name: Fatty Fish
description: Fatty fish (such as salmon, mackerel, and sardines) are unparalleled therapeutic superfoods. Providing a combination of highly bioavailable proteins, substantial amounts of active Vitamin D3, and profound concentrations of omega-3 fatty acids, they serve as the gold standard for cardiovascular and neural health.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Provides clean, sustained cellular energy driven primarily by high-quality proteins and healthy structural fats.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: An elite, highly bioavailable complete protein source containing all essential amino acids required for muscle synthesis and metabolic repair.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Rich in vital polyunsaturated fats, specifically the anti-inflammatory omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Completely clear of carbohydrates, making it an ideal whole food for stabilizing insulin and supporting low-glycemic dietary goals.

microNutrients.name: Omega-3 (EPA/DHA)
microNutrients.description: Essential long-chain fatty acids that construct healthy brain cell membranes, optimize lipid panels, and dramatically reduce systemic arterial inflammation.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin D3 (Cholecalciferol)
microNutrients.description: One of the absolute richest natural dietary sources of active Vitamin D3, foundational for systemic calcium absorption and immune system performance.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B12
microNutrients.description: Critical nutrient for maintaining the nervous system, securing neurological processing speed, and driving red blood cell production.

microNutrients.name: Selenium
microNutrients.description: A major trace antioxidant that activates enzymes to safeguard arterial linings and shield the thyroid gland from oxidative stress.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: An essential intracellular mineral that works in sync with sodium to regulate cellular fluid pump mechanics and manage resting blood pressure.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B6
microNutrients.description: Serves as a crucial metabolic coenzyme involved in cellular protein processing and the natural synthesis of cognitive neurotransmitters.

healthBenefits: Cardiovascular Smoothness & Architecture: The heavy input of marine EPA and DHA lowers blood triglycerides, optimizes arterial elasticity, reduces resting blood pressure, and helps stabilize heart rhythms.

Advanced Cognitive Optimization: Since DHA is a primary structural lipid component of the human brain cortex, consistent consumption preserves optimal neuro-signaling, boosts memory parameters, and mitigates age-related cognitive decline.

Powerful Systemic Anti-Inflammation: Marine omega-3 fats directly compete with inflammatory pathways, drastically decreasing the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and protecting metabolic tissues.
Skeletal & Immune Reinforcement: Exceptional natural concentrations of active Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) maximize intestinal calcium absorption, consolidating skeletal bone density matrices.
precautions: Mercury & Heavy Metal Bioaccumulation: Large predatory fish species (like swordfish, king mackerel, and large tuna) can accumulate mercury in their muscle tissue over time. For frequent eating, choose smaller species like salmon, sardines, or trout.

Environmental Pollutant Thresholds: Wild-caught fish from heavily industrialized water bodies may contain trace persistent organic pollutants (POPs) or PCBs. Sourcing your seafood from certified, environmentally sustainable fisheries is highly advised.

Fish and Seafood Allergies: Fish allergy is highly prevalent and typically persists throughout adulthood, carrying a high risk of triggering severe, immediate anaphylactic reactions in sensitive individuals.

Perishability & Histamine Toxicity: If fatty fish is stored incorrectly or sits too long before freezing, the rapid bacterial breakdown of histidine can cause high histamine accumulation, leading to scombroid food poisoning.
